components.basis: Present: the tuple (V,H,M,T) with finite V, H and M subsets of V, finite T over V, empty sets allowed (parts 21-34); the source's consistent-T requirement and the flagged inconsistent-T extension (parts 13-16); both omitted restrictions with the source's reason for each and its remark about its proofs (parts 34-49); positive-atom restriction with Konolige [40] and the x'<->F reduction, proved with inclusion and cardinality preserved (parts 50-60, 230-263; annex 288-335); no special form of T, the clausal-form remark and its complexity claim attributed to the source, with the semantic clausal-equivalence fact proved (parts 61-72, 186-228; annex 396-455); the source's theory vocabulary of manuscript p. 9 (parts 142-184); candidates restricted to subsets of H (parts 79-82); worked boundary inputs with empty data, inconsistent T and an entailing atom outside H (parts 577-599).
components.gap: Narrowed source claim (manuscript p. 10, first remark after def. 2.2): the source says that in this model a hypothesis plays the role of what in other models is called an abducible proposition, pointing to Console, Theseider Dupre and Torasso, 'On the Relationship Between Abduction and Deduction', Journal of Logic and Computation 1(5), 1991 (its reference [14], PDF p. 42). The entry renders this only as H 'also called the abducible atoms' (parts lines 26-27), dropping that the term belongs to other models and the source's reference; no other handbook file states it. Owed: state in independent wording that the hypotheses of this model play the role that other models (e.g. Console, Theseider Dupre and Torasso) call abducible propositions, with that reference.

components.basis: Truth values, Val(V), local satisfaction, Mod_V, consistency as satisfiability, Gamma entails M for every member, the explanation condition and Expl(P) identified with the source's Sol(P) of def. 2.2 (parts 86-116); the identification with the book's consequence relation is proved (annex 13-33); worked boundary: inconsistent background and empty data (parts 604-613, annex 186-208).

Statement covers the finite criterion, agreement with valuations on all of Prop, exact agreement with defs. 2.1-2.2 for consistent T after naming and abbreviation expansion, and the three boundary cases (inconsistent T, empty explanation, empty M). Annex proof writes every step: coincidence induction, local/global countervaluations, the notation translation (truth constant, biconditional, naming preserving inclusion and cardinality), and each boundary case including empty V.

Vacuous entailment from inconsistency, one model versus every model, a single countervaluation, and membership in H as a separate restriction are stated (parts 265-277); the three failures are worked with written calculations: P_inconsistent, P_constraint ({b} consistent and non-entailing, {a,b} inconsistent) and P_permitted ({z} outside H) (annex 186-191, 238-267).

MinExpl and CardExpl defined, empty when no explanation, no probability/cost/causal content (parts 282-305). Source variants of def. 2.3 and the following discussion (manuscript pp. 10-11): preference as a preorder on 2^H justified by reflexivity and transitivity, strict part, Sol_preceq as prec-minimal solutions, the =, subset and size orders with [59], irredundancy (def. 2.4) with proper inclusion and its sources [59,69,6,40], subset order as irredundancy itself (parts 344-392); derivation of both families from def. 2.3, Sol = Sol_=, irredundancy of subset and size orders, failure for equality on P_given, and irredundant preferences selecting subset-minimal solutions, all proved (parts 394-431, annex 457-506). Worked boundary: P_sizes, {b,c} subset-minimal but not of minimum size.

Existence of a subset-minimal explanation inside every explanation, nonemptiness of both families, CardExpl within MinExpl within Expl, incomparability with possibly different sizes, the single-deletion characterization (source prop. 2.1, both directions, extended to inconsistent T) and qualified monotonicity are stated (parts 307-337) and proved step by step, including the consistency step the source's proof leaves implicit and the empty-explanation case (annex 71-126). Worked boundary: sizes one and two in P_sizes; inconsistent superset {a,b} in P_constraint.

Input, fixed listing order, candidate enumeration, per-candidate valuation scan with two flags, append rule, subset filter, minimum-cardinality filter including the empty case, and the boundary of zero-length vectors (empty H, empty V, empty M) are all written.

Termination, exact equality of the three outputs with Expl, MinExpl and CardExpl, absence of duplicates, the 2^(r+n) pair count and the disclaimer of unit-cost or complexity claims are stated; the proof writes the vector bijections and counts, the flag invariants by induction, soundness and completeness, both filters, and termination including inconsistent and empty inputs.
Six tuples with distinctness convention and tuple order stated, declared as handbook examples (not attributed to the source).

All three families for each of the six inputs are stated and computed in full: every candidate is checked for consistency and entailment with an explicit model or countervaluation, the exact criterion for P_sizes is proved in both directions, and the minimality families are derived.

Statement with the explicit countervaluation, written proof extending it to the book's global semantics, and the interpretive limitation (explanation is conditional; declared observations and background are not thereby evidenced).

Material reading of the arrows, absence of causal, interventional, temporal and probabilistic structure, and the insufficiency of minimality for causal claims are stated; the worked boundary (two finite SCMs with the same compatible valuations, the same explanation families and opposite intervention behaviour, plus the shared countervaluation) is stated and proved with every model and intervention computed; scope pointers resolve to existing labels.

duties.duty: Whole required source extent selected by the chapter locator (parts line 9 and annex line 7: EiterGottlobAbductionManuscript sec. 2, manuscript pp. 9-11 = held PDF pp. 10-12, i.e. the 'Abduction model' and 'The main problems' subsections), compared item by item with the handbook route: every hypothesis and variant, every promised case, every example, every justificatory, historical or normative claim.
duties.basis: Present at the cited lines: language and theory conventions, the theory as a conjunction, literal/clause/Horn/definite Horn/clausal form/CNF/DNF vocabulary, truth assignments and the substitution E_phi(X) with a proved value lemma (manuscript p. 9); defs. 2.1-2.2 with the consistent-T variant; the H-M overlap and non-exhaustion remarks with reasons and the remark about the source's proofs; positive atoms with [40] and the x'<->F reduction proved; no special form, the clausal-form complexity remark, and p. 8's clausal summary; preorders justified by reflexivity and transitivity, strict part, def. 2.3, Sol = Sol_=, irredundancy with [59,69,6,40], def. 2.4, the subset and size orders with [59] (p. 10); prop. 2.1 with written proof; lem. 2.2 with written proof and a counterexample without disjointness; the three main problems; the complexity-subject sentence; def. 2.5; the three-set division (shown to need nonempty acceptable solutions); irrelevance and dispensability with [36]; the prefix convention; the dispensability focus (p. 11). Every locator in the chapter was opened in the held source and shows the cited content.
duties.gap: Omitted historical claim, manuscript p. 11 ('The main problems'): right after saying that the complexity of the three problems is its main subject, the source states that deciding relevance or necessity of hypotheses had previously been dealt with by Bylander, Allemang, Tanner and Josephson for set-oriented abduction models (its reference [5], 'Some Results Concerning the Computational Complexity of Abduction', KR-89) and by Selman and Levesque [69] (AAAI-90), Friedrich, Gottlob and Nejdl [28] (1990) and Bylander [4] (KR-91) for certain subclasses of propositional abduction (references at PDF pp. 42-46). def:p15-w02c-p15-027-relevance (parts lines 457-486) reproduces the surrounding text but not this claim, and no other handbook file states it. Owed: state this prior-work claim with its four sources. The narrowed abducible-proposition remark of p. 10 ([14]) is a second omission in this extent, charged to C001.

defect_observations: Not counted as a gap (a statement of the source's own focus, not a justificatory, historical or normative claim): the source's sentences at manuscript pp. 10-11, 'We will mainly deal with irredundant preference orders in this paper' and 'Both orders will deserve proper attention in our study', are not reported; the irredundancy of the subset and size orders itself is proved (thm:p15-w02c-p15-027-preference item 3). Adding them with the two owed items would complete the extent verbatim in substance.

Fidelity note (coverage unaffected): parts lines 40-42 render the source's 'our results remain valid under both restrictions' as 'remain valid when either restriction is imposed'; the source's next sentences treat each restriction separately, so the reading is defensible.

Fidelity note (coverage unaffected): parts lines 53-54 describe Konolige's reference [40] as a paper 'on abduction and closure in causal theories'; its title is 'Abduction versus closure in causal theories' (Artificial Intelligence 53, 1992; source PDF p. 44).
